cardSummary: Acreages, hobby farms and a long exposed shoreline, where tree permits take weeks and must be posted before work.
intro: North Saanich is acreage country with a long shoreline: hobby farms and rural lots around Ardmore and McDonald Park, waterfront homes from Deep Cove to Lands End and Curteis Point, and townhouse stratas near Dean Park.

The Tree Protection Bylaw (No. 1548) needs a permit to remove a regulated tree, generally from 20 cm across and smaller for native species. Topping is prohibited. Staff review takes about two to three weeks and the permit must be posted 48 hours before work, so removals need planning. See [tree and vegetation work](/services/tree-vegetation/) or [request a free quote](/free-quote/?area=north-saanich).
localRulesIntro: In North Saanich, timing is the main thing to plan for: allow for staff review and the 48-hour posting before any regulated removal. In environmental and steep-slope permit areas, trees are regulated from 10 cm.

localNotes.title: North Saanich Tree Protection Bylaw
localNotes.text: North Saanich's Tree Protection Bylaw No. 1548 requires a permit to remove any regulated tree (generally 20 cm diameter or more, smaller for arbutus, Garry oak, Pacific dogwood, yew and shore pine, plus trees in environmental or steep-slope areas). Topping is prohibited; best-practice pruning needs no permit. Staff review takes about 2-3 weeks and the permit must be posted 48 hours before work.

localNotes.title: CRD lawn-watering schedule
localNotes.text: CRD Stage 1 watering rules run May 1 to September 30 for properties on the regional water supply: lawns may be watered on Wednesdays and Saturdays (even addresses) or Thursdays and Sundays (odd addresses), 4-10 am or 7-10 pm; hand watering and drip irrigation of trees, shrubs and gardens is allowed any day. Multi-unit complexes use the complex's street address. New sod or seed does not need a permit and has a temporary schedule.

localNotes.title: Invasive plants and disposal
localNotes.text: The CRD Regional Invasive Species Program lists priority species (including giant hogweed, knotweed, gorse, poison hemlock, shiny geranium and yellow toadflax) and asks for sightings to be reported. Invasive plants must be disposed of properly: Hartland Landfill takes them bagged and labelled or in covered loads, and knotweed needs a controlled waste permit and is not accepted at municipal yard-waste drop-offs.

conditions.title: Wind and salt on the shoreline
conditions.body: Waterfront lots at Lands End, Curteis Point and Deep Cove face open water and winter storms. Salt-tolerant hedging and wind-firm planting last longer there.

conditions.title: Deer and open acreage
conditions.body: Deer are common across rural North Saanich. Vegetable gardens and new planting usually need fencing or deer-resistant choices.

conditions.title: Wells and the regional supply
conditions.body: Some rural properties may be on private wells rather than the regional supply. The CRD lawn days apply only where you are connected, but well owners still benefit from low-flow drip.

conditions.title: Lower thresholds near slopes and streams
conditions.body: In environmental and steep-slope development permit areas, trees from 10 cm are regulated, so clearing on those parts of a lot needs a check first.

topServices.why: Large lawns, rough grass, hedges and fence lines on acreage need a steady seasonal routine.
Removals have to be scheduled around permit review and posting, and careful reduction pruning stays clear of the topping ban.

servicesBlurb.grounds-maintenance: Acreage upkeep: lawns, rough mowing, hedges and fence lines.
servicesBlurb.landscape-installation: Gardens for waterfront and rural homes, with deer and wind in mind.
servicesBlurb.irrigation: Irrigation for large lawns and beds, including drip for hedgerows.
servicesBlurb.tree-vegetation: Removals timed around permit review, and best-practice pruning.

jobNotes.title: Removal booked around the permit clock
jobNotes.body: A regulated tree removal was scheduled three weeks out to allow for staff review, and the crew start was set after the 48-hour posting period.

jobNotes.title: Reduction cuts instead of topping
jobNotes.body: Overgrown trees along a strata boundary were reduced with selective cuts over two seasons rather than topped, which the bylaw does not allow.

cta.heading: Get a free quote in North Saanich
cta.body: If you need a tree removed, tell us early: permit review and posting add a few weeks. For acreage care, let us know the rough size of the lot.
